intent: Charter gate asks for one owning charter per INDEX row, not every listed one
notes: The `charter-index-gap` commit check required every charter on every `INDEX.md` row that matched a changed file (#18). `INDEX.md` is a reading list, so routine UI-only, server-only and one-module changes needed either a no-op charter edit or an Architect approval, and almost every row pushed notes into the always-read Cross-Cutting charter.

Now each matching row needs at least one of its domain charters. Cross-Cutting counts as a domain charter only on a row that lists nothing else. Otherwise it is required only for a file its own `Covers` line names, matched with the same `Covers` grammar the charter verifier uses. The failure still blocks with an external approval, and a code change with no charter update at all is still blocked as before.
The message names what is missing: "INDEX.md routes <files> to A or B; update at least one of them." or "<Cross-Cutting> covers <files>; update it."

The shared `Covers` matcher (`charter_covers.py`) now ships in both hook runtimes, byte-identical with the verifier's copy. The Enterprise hook copy has the same change. `INDEX.md` row matching itself is unchanged.

Architect decision: the middle option from #18. The significance steelman is in the session record: a real cross-layer change can now pass with one charter, and Cross-Cutting loses its forcing function for contracts in files it does not cover.
